name: Matthieu Valet - Projet de décision du Conseil
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion of the Agreement between the European Union, of the one part, and the Republic of Ecuador, of the other part, on cooperation between the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) and the Ecuadorian authorities competent for combating serious crime and terrorism
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees that the European Union should sign a cooperation agreement with Ecuador on fighting serious crime and terrorism. The deal lets Europol, the European Union's law enforcement agency, share personal data with Ecuador's authorities. Supporters say this is needed because criminal networks traffic drugs, people and arms across borders, and cooperation without data sharing is weak. The agreement also sets data protection rules and safeguards for people's privacy. The Parliament's role is to give or refuse consent; it gives its consent.

- Europol and Ecuador can now exchange personal data, with data protection safeguards, to fight serious crime and terrorism.
- It affects law enforcement authorities in the European Union and Ecuador, and people whose data is shared.
- The Parliament has consented; the Council can now conclude the agreement.
